description: How much will average DRAM (including HBM) contract prices rise in calendar 2026, as Nvidia reports substantially higher memory and component costs across the industry?
outcome: The change in average DRAM/HBM contract prices in calendar 2026 versus calendar 2025, per TrendForce/DRAMeXchange data.
period: Calendar year 2026 — the item's present-tense 'ongoing memory shortage' and Nvidia's statement that memory costs 'have increased substantially' (article dated 2 October 2026); checked against TrendForce/DRAMeXchange full-year 2026 DRAM contract price data (expected early 2027).

description: How much venture funding will physical AI (robotics) companies raise globally in calendar 2026?
outcome: Total global venture capital raised by physical AI/robotics startups in calendar 2026, versus the $28.7 billion raised in all of 2025 and the $33.4 billion already raised in the first half of 2026, per PitchBook data.
period: Calendar year 2026, checked at PitchBook's full-year 2026 venture funding release (expected early 2027); the item gives H1 2026 and full-year 2025 figures only.

description: How much will the five largest AI hyperscalers spend in total on data centers in calendar 2027?
outcome: The big five AI hyperscalers' combined calendar-2027 data-center capital expenditure, versus the $1.3 trillion Nvidia projects for next year (as cited in the item) and the nearly $800 billion expected for calendar 2026.
period: Calendar year 2027, checked at the hyperscalers' 2027 capex guidance from their October 2026 earnings and at their Q4/full-year 2027 earnings and capex disclosures in early 2028.

description: Will Nvidia's co-packaged-optics (CPO) switch shipments reach volume in calendar 2027 — approaching the 30,000 units by mid-2027 and the 100,000 units for the full year that GF Securities forecasts?
outcome: Nvidia's CPO switch shipment volume from Q4 2026 through calendar 2027 (GF Securities: 15,000 units in Q4 2026, 16,000 in early 2027, 30,000 by mid-2027, 100,000 for all of 2027), as reflected in Nvidia's networking revenue disclosures and suppliers' CPO/NPO laser shipments.
period: Calendar 2027, with the item's stated checkpoints at Q4 2026, early 2027 and mid-2027, checked against Nvidia's quarterly results and supplier disclosures. The item gives no confirmation date, so the forecast periods it states fix the check dates.

description: Will the combined data center capital expenditures of the 'big four' AI hyperscalers for calendar 2026 come in near the ~$650 billion the item reports they plan to spend?
outcome: The big four AI hyperscalers' aggregated calendar-2026 data center capital expenditure versus the ~$650 billion plan reported in the item, with Nvidia's own projection of ~$1 trillion for 2027 as the forward reference.
period: Full-year calendar 2026, checked against the hyperscalers' capex disclosures in their Q4 2026 earnings reports (reported roughly January–February 2027); the item gives no release date, so the check date is set by the companies' own year-end reporting.

description: Will NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture, designed to house its 2027 Rubin Ultra chips, reach revenue-generating first shipments in calendar 2027 as originally planned, or slip to 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
outcome: Whether the Kyber rack debuts and ships with Vera Rubin Ultra in calendar 2027 (consistent with NVIDIA's 'roadmap is intact') or is delayed to 2028 (SemiAnalysis), and when first shipments actually occur.
period: Calendar 2027 first shipments — the item says Kyber 'had been slated to debut with Vera Rubin Ultra ... in 2027' and reports a >12-month delay to 2028; whether 2027 shipments occur can be checked at year-end 2027, with 2028 as the reported slip date.

description: Will NVIDIA's Vera Rubin Ultra / Kyber NVL144 rack-scale system begin shipping to customers by the end of calendar 2028, following SemiAnalysis's report that its debut slipped from 2027 to 2028 (which NVIDIA disputes, saying its roadmap is intact)?
outcome: First customer shipments of the Kyber rack-scale architecture (NVL144) with Vera Rubin Ultra, confirmed by NVIDIA.
period: 2028-12-31 (the item says the Kyber debut was pushed to 2028 from a 2027 plan; the check date is the end of that year. If NVIDIA's 'roadmap is intact,' shipping in 2027 would also settle the by-end-2028 question affirmatively.)

description: Will DRAM/HBM contract prices remain elevated through calendar 2027, extending the shortage that has raised GPU makers' memory input costs?
outcome: Direction and level of DRAM/HBM contract prices through calendar 2027, specifically whether they remain above 2026 levels or normalize as Micron's 2027/2028 outlook suggests.
period: Full-year calendar 2027; checked against Q4 2027 DRAM contract price releases (TrendForce/DRAMeXchange) and memory makers' Q4 2027 results, reported roughly January 2028.

description: Will Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture, the rack system slated to debut with its Vera Rubin Ultra generation, reach first customer shipments, and in which year — 2027 as originally slated or 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
outcome: First customer shipments of Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack architecture (Vera Rubin Ultra generation), confirmed by the company, versus the reported more-than-12-month delay to 2028.
period: 2028 — the date SemiAnalysis reports for Kyber's delayed debut, against the original 2027 schedule stated in the item; checked against Nvidia's quarterly reports and management confirmation of initial Kyber/Rubin Ultra shipments.

description: Will Nvidia actually resume selling H200 AI chips into China by Nvidia's FY2027 year-end — i.e., will Beijing permit Chinese commercial users to buy the chips the U.S. cleared for export in December 2025?
outcome: Whether H200 sales to Chinese customers take place (China data-center revenue returning above zero) versus Beijing keeping Nvidia locked out despite the U.S. approval.
period: Nvidia's FY2027 year-end (late January 2027) — set by the reason: a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end.

description: Will Nvidia's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture — the rack system that houses its Rubin Ultra generation, the generation after Vera Rubin — reach first shipments in 2028, after SemiAnalysis reported the program has slipped more than 12 months from a planned 2027 debut?
outcome: First shipments of the Kyber NVL144 rack system (Rubin Ultra generation) in 2028 versus the original 2027 schedule, and whether the larger NVL576 multi-rack system ships in volume at all.
period: First shipments by end of calendar 2028 — set by the item: SemiAnalysis says the Kyber NVL144 architecture 'has been delayed to 2028' from a planned 2027 debut alongside Rubin Ultra.

description: How far will the US crackdown on advanced AI-chip exports to third countries escalate — will the US Commerce Department go beyond its May 2026 guidance and impose formal licensing requirements or other escalated restrictions on AI-chip shipments to third countries such as Malaysia, Singapore and Japan by Nvidia's FY2027 year-end?
outcome: Whether the US Commerce Department / Bureau of Industry and Security moves beyond its May 2026 guidance to a binding export-licensing rule or other escalated restriction on AI-chip shipments to third countries, and the resulting constraint on Nvidia's sales to those markets.
period: Nvidia's FY2027 year-end (late January 2027) — set by the reason: a pending regulatory decision is tracked to the current fiscal year-end.

description: Will NVIDIA's Vera Rubin next-generation AI chip platform, the product line that carries its data center value, begin shipping by a check date (end of calendar 2026)?
outcome: Confirmation that first Vera Rubin shipments have begun, versus slipping into 2027 or later.
period: First shipments by end of calendar 2026 — set by the item: the platform 'could begin shipping later this year' in an article dated 2 July 2026.

description: What will the big four AI hyperscalers' combined data center capital expenditures be in calendar 2027, and will they approach the roughly $1 trillion level Nvidia projects for next year?
outcome: The combined 2027 data center capex of the big four AI hyperscalers, measured against Nvidia's ~$1 trillion projection and the 2026 level of ~$650 billion.
period: Calendar 2027 — set by the item: Nvidia projects hyperscaler capex could reach $1 trillion 'next year' in an article dated 4 July 2026.

description: What will contract prices for AI memory (LPDDR5X, HBM, 3D NAND/DRAM) be through calendar 2026-2027 — the input that now makes up roughly 25-30% of Nvidia's Vera Rubin rack cost?
outcome: The level and direction of contract memory (DRAM, NAND, HBM) prices in 2026-2027 and the resulting per-rack memory content cost (about $2 million on the VR200).
period: Calendar 2026-2027 memory contract cycles; set by the item's forward cost period (second half of 2026 and beyond).

description: Will NAND demand generated by Nvidia's CMX (Context Memory Storage) architecture, the storage tier built around its BlueField-4 DPU for long-context and agentic inference, exceed 100 million TB in calendar 2027, up from a projected 35 million TB in 2026?
outcome: The volume of NAND demand attributable to Nvidia's CMX architecture in calendar 2027, against the item's projection of more than 100 million TB (from 35 million TB in 2026), and whether memory makers' capacity additions keep pace with it.
period: Calendar 2027 with calendar 2026 as base year; settled when full-year 2027 NAND demand/bit-shipment data for CMX are published (early 2028, e.g. TrendForce releases and memory makers' 2027 reports).

description: Will NVIDIA's Rubin Ultra rack-scale platform — the Kyber NVL144 architecture that houses 144 Rubin Ultra GPUs — reach first shipments in 2027 as originally planned, or slip to 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
outcome: Whether NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 / Rubin Ultra rack platform reaches first shipments (the step that brings revenue) in 2027 or is delayed to 2028.
period: 2028 — the release date SemiAnalysis reports Kyber has been pushed to from an original 2027; the question is settled when Kyber NVL144 / Rubin Ultra first ships (the item supports the original-2027-vs-2028 timing).

description: Will NVIDIA's Kyber NVL144 rack-scale architecture — the rack system designed to house its 2027 Rubin Ultra chips — begin shipping by end-2027 as originally scheduled, or has it slipped to 2028 as SemiAnalysis reports?
outcome: First shipments of the Kyber NVL144 rack-scale system (paired with Rubin Ultra), confirmed by NVIDIA disclosure or an official shipment announcement, occurring in 2027 versus slipping to 2028.
period: 2027-12-31 check date — the item (published 2026-07-05) says Kyber was slated to debut with Vera Rubin Ultra in 2027 and has been delayed by more than 12 months to 2028, so end-2027 discriminates the original schedule from the reported delay.

description: How much will the big four AI hyperscalers spend on data-center capital expenditures in calendar 2026, and does their combined spend approach the ~$1 trillion level NVIDIA projects for 2027?
outcome: Combined calendar-2026 data-center capital expenditure of the big four AI hyperscalers, measured against the ~$650 billion plan reported in the item and NVIDIA's ~$1 trillion projection for 2027.
period: Calendar year 2026, settled by the hyperscalers' Q4 2026 earnings and capex disclosures (reported early 2027).

description: Will server DRAM prices jump another 260% in calendar 2026, after rising 64% in the second half of 2025, as the item projects?
outcome: The change in server DRAM prices for calendar 2026 versus the prior period, as measured by industry server DRAM price data.
period: Calendar 2026; checked against server DRAM price reports for 2026 (e.g., TrendForce/DRAMeXchange quarterly updates) after the year or in periodic releases. The item states the 2026 projection.

description: How many advanced AI accelerators will Huawei, together with its chipmaking partner SMIC, produce in calendar 2026 (combined Huawei-designed Ascend output: 910B, 910C and the new 950PR line)?
outcome: The combined 2026 output of Huawei-designed AI chips manufactured at SMIC, in units, measured against the contested estimates in circulation (Nvidia's report: SMIC above 700,000 Ascend 910C by end-2026 at a 50,000-per-month run rate and several million 910B in 2027; Commerce Secretary Lutnick: 200,000 advanced chips for 2025; Chris McGuire: 800,000 910C in 2025, 2 million in 2026 and 4 million in 2027 as stress cases).
period: Calendar 2026 — set by the item's SMIC capacity figures ('by the end of this year ... 50,000 of these chips per month').

description: How much will global AI capital spending total in calendar 2026 and calendar 2027?
outcome: Global AI capex for calendar 2026 and calendar 2027, measured against Goldman Sachs' forecast of $1 trillion of global AI spend this year and AI spend equal to 1.8% of U.S. GDP in 2026, 2.5% in 2027 (and 2.8% in 2028).
period: Calendar 2026 and calendar 2027 (with 2028 also given), the years Goldman Sachs' forecast in the Oct. 11, 2026 article covers.

description: How much combined capital expenditure will the five largest hyperscalers — Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta Platforms and Oracle — spend in calendar 2026 and calendar 2027?
outcome: The big five hyperscalers' combined capex for calendar 2026 and calendar 2027, versus the approximately $800 billion for 2026 and roughly $1.3 trillion for 2027 the article reports they plan to spend.
period: Calendar 2026 and calendar 2027 (the two years the Oct. 6, 2026 article gives), settled at the hyperscalers' quarterly earnings releases reporting capex through the fourth quarter of 2027.
